text:
sara_support: FYI escalation from customer. They started hitting sudden 429s and occasional 401s after switching to rwd-instruct-48k with large contexts (~48k tokens) + parallel embed calls. Customer reports exact error: 'rate limit exceeded' + header snippets. Sharing the repro and headers below.

rate-limiter-bot: automated: request_id=abcde-17865-01, status=429, reason=RATE_LIMIT, suggested_retry=120s

aaron_se: can you paste the customer's exact curl and the throttle headers? also which region and API key (masked) were used?

sara_support: pasted from the customer (they asked to keep key masked):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-XXXXxx" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-instruct-48k","input":"<~48k context>","max_tokens":1024}'
```

They also sent these response headers from a 429: 

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rwd-rpm-limit: 1500
x-rwd-rpm-remaining: 0
x-rwd-concurrency-limit: 12
x-rwd-concurrency-used: 12
x-rwd-trace-id: abcdef123456
x-rwd-quota-policy: per-model
```

sara_support: they said this happens when their client fanouts: one generate + 3 parallel embed calls per user request. They batch 40 users concurrently in a single process.

miguel_eng: thanks — that header set is helpful. initial read: per-model RPM=1500 and concurrency cap=12 for rwd-instruct-48k in that region. Two immediate things stand out:
- heavy fanout (1 gen + 3 embeds) multiplies RPM pressure per logical user.
- long contexts increase per-request token accounting, and our token-cost estimator increases effective RPM consumption for large-context models.

miguel_eng: quick Qs for repro: can you ask them to share a trace id for a 401 (if they have one) and whether the 401 coincides with 429s or is separate? also which client library and version?

sara_support: asked customer to give a 401 trace; they replied with one trace id: trace=abcdef123457. client is node 0.12 (custom wrapper), region=us-west-2.

miguel_eng: ok i'll try to reproduce locally with their pattern. Could you also ask them if they use emb batching or send separate embed calls per item?

sara_support: they said "separate" — they call embed endpoint per item (3 per request) rather than batching.

miguel_eng: that explains a lot. Separate embed calls per user x 40 concurrent users = 120 extra embed requests in parallel. With concurrency=12 we hit hard caps quickly and the rate limiter will return 429s. 401s likely from a downstream auth throttle when retries overlap, will dig in.

olivia_billing: noted billing check: I don't see an invoice-level overage yet, but if they retry aggressively we might see a burst usage spike. I'll hold off until eng confirms pattern.

miguel_eng: plan: reproduce with a small script that launches 40 workers, each does [generate + 3 embed calls] concurrently. If I can reproduce, we'll: (1) adjust per-model burst window accounting to treat embed+generate fanout more conservatively for large-context models, (2) propose short-term config: reduce concurrency for that API key to 6 or enable per-key queuing, (3) recommend customer batching.

sara_support: can you post the repro script here so customer can run it in a staging environment? they asked to validate before we change any server config.

miguel_eng: dropping a minimal python repro for them: 

```python
# repro.py — spawns N workers doing 1 gen + 3 embeds
import requests, threading, time
API='https://api.redwood.ai/v1'
HEAD={'Authorization':'Bearer sk-REDACTED','Content-Type':'application/json'}

def worker(i):
    # generate
    requests.post(API+'/generate', headers=HEAD, json={"model":"rwd-instruct-48k","input":"x'*20000","max_tokens":512})
    # 3 parallel embed calls
    for _ in range(3):
        requests.post(API+'/embed', headers=HEAD, json={"model":"rwd-embed-4k","input":"short text"})

threads=[]
for i in range(40):
    t=threading.Thread(target=worker, args=(i,))
    t.start()
    threads.append(t)

for t in threads:
    t.join()
```

miguel_eng: if they can run that in staging and reproduce, include one 429 response (full headers + body) and the trace id. we'll use that to tune the limiter.

aaron_se: short-term mitigation we can tell them: 1) batch embeds (send array) 2) cap client concurrency to <=6 3) add exponential backoff with jitter on 429s 4) reduce max_tokens in generation when possible.

sara_support: shared mitigation steps to customer. they replied "ok will try batching and re-test" and asked if we can temporarily raise their per-model concurrency while they migrate.

miguel_eng: temporary raise possible but will require approval & we need to ensure it won't impact other tenants. I'll open an internal ticket against the rate limiter to evaluate a per-key temporary bump (+verify isolation) and include a regen of the token-cost multiplier for long contexts.

olivia_billing: if we do a temporary bump we should flag the account to prevent unexpected billing spikes; I'll create a billing watch and notify finance for potential credits if needed.

miguel_eng: reproduced locally — 429s appear at similar concurrency, trace id for local test: local-trace-17865-xyz. Root cause: token bucket exhaustion + concurrency cap, exacerbated by separate embed calls. We'll add a heuristic to multiply token-cost by fanout factor for a single API key (embeds+generate) until they batch.

miguel_eng: action items:
- eng: open RATE-3123 to add fanout-aware accounting + per-key temporary bump path (assigned to me)
- eng-oncall: evaluate safe bump for this customer's key (ETA 24h)
- support: advise customer to batch embeds + add client-side cap to 6 concurrent workers immediately
- billing: place account on watch for spike and hold auto-invoicing adjustments

sara_support: acked and will keep customer updated. marking as high-priority escalation.

miguel_eng: I'll push a small config change to staging that reduces effective concurrency for rwd-instruct-48k while we test the fanout heuristic. Will update thread when it's deployed.

sara_support: thanks — please ping me when staging change is live so I can coordinate customer test.

olivia_billing: created billing watch and note linked to RATE-3123.

sara_support: closing loop once we confirm customer repro test or do a temporary bump.

miguel_eng: assigned. keeping thread open for traces.
